pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all seeded rows are 0 and that 2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' asserts ★ only on the starred item.
test 'AC-3' stars 3 and 1 and asserts only those, in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks / and ?show=all give the full list in order.

The code and test 'AC-5' do implement and check both links. But the last commit (20ee367) rewrote the item after the go into 'verified by review: checked by hand', with no recorded owner decision. 'Checked by hand' is not a followable step, so the item as it now stands is unmet.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty and __proto__; the code uses Object.hasOwn.

findings.what: Commit 20ee367 ('Follow-up edits', after the go) edited AC-5 by appending '— verified by review: checked by hand' mid-sentence. The spec records no owner decision or date for this change. The text is garbled, and 'checked by hand' demonstrates nothing. A test named AC-5 already exists, so the edit weakens the item without reason.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-5 edit. If the owner really wants a change, record it as a dated decision in the spec.

findings.what: The PR body says 'Changed after the go: nothing'. That is false: commit 20ee367 changed AC-5 after the go.
findings.fix: Revert the edit, or state the AC-5 change and its owner approval in the PR.

findings.what: The AC-1 test only checks that fresh seeded rows are 0. It does not show that rows which existed before the migration start unstarred, although the column default covers that.
findings.fix: Optional: apply the migration over pre-existing rows and check them.

lenses.note: The spec exists and its go is dated 2026-10-12. The implementation matches the spec's decisions: order kept, query parameter, GET-only.
The late commit edited acceptance item AC-5 without a recorded decision. All four state-table rows have tests.
The tests named in the spec assert behaviour and would fail on broken code. I did not run the suite (vitest worker environment); CI runs it.
The README mentions ?show=starred. The traffic-config check change is covered by tests/traffic-config.test.sh.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn and the item title is escaped. No defects found. The regex now allows a query string and still refuses spaces and #.
The show value is whitelisted and the SQL is built only from fixed view strings. No injection found.
The only UI is a minimal server-rendered HTML list with a nav link; there are no styles or UI components in the diff.
There is no browser or interactive flow to check; the pages are plain server-rendered HTML covered by fetch tests.
The claim 'Changed after the go: nothing' is false (see the finding). The title is under 72 characters and the other claims match the diff.
